CMAA 5001.title: Foundations of Computational Media and Arts
CMAA 5001.description: This course introduces students to the conceptual fundamentals of computational media and arts, technologies behind computational media and arts, and software and hardware tools used in computational media and arts production. It will cover principles of visual communication, design aesthetics, image and video synthesis, audio editing, animation and game design, etc.
cilos: Explain the history of CMA.
Demonstrate the knowledge of the major forms and technologies of CMA.
Use open-source CMA tools.
Apply critical thinking and communication skills.
Apply artistic creation skills.

CMAA 5002.title: Animation Art: From Concept to Production
CMAA 5002.description: From screenplay through post-production, students are immersed in the collaborative animation pipeline. In this course, students will utilize a variety of animation tools and techniques to tell a compelling story and experience the diverse roles within the animation industry through storyboarding, editing and completion of a short animated film.
cilos: Demonstrate proficiency in applying abilities to an animation production pipeline.
Exhibit professionalism in directing a team or being directed as an artist.
Demonstrate commitment to completing the project to the highest possible standard.
Structure a compelling story and create a unique visual aesthetic through pre-production materials.
Assume a variety of production roles to achieve production deadlines and complete a fully animated, rendered and polished sequence.
Complete the post-production process, including compositing, editing and sound design.

CMAA 5003.title: Virtual Production Studio
CMAA 5003.description: This course explores the creative power and expressions in visual storytelling and cinematic production with real-time rendering technology, LED-based virtual production, Gen AI and other digital tools. Students will learn and apply creative arts and principles of storytelling and filmmaking and integrate them in real-time virtual platform with virtual assets and characters. This course prepares and equips students with the soft and hard skills for endless creative possibilities in virtual production and visual content creation.

CMAA 5007.title: Computational Approach to Chinese Calligraphy
CMAA 5007.description: This course covers the most fundamental knowledge and techniques of Chinese calligraphy and its important role in the modern technological advances. The history and various styles of calligraphy, history and principles of making rice paper, seal making and its role, and best-known calligraphers are introduced. Students will first learn and practice writing Chinese calligraphy on rice paper and then use deep learning tools to transfer interesting calligraphy styles. Students will develop projects, such as programming to generate or drive robots to write calligraphy. There will be guest lectures by well-known Chinese calligraphers and researchers in digitizing and modernizing Chinese calligraphy. A trip is planned to visit the best-known rice paper factory (红星宣纸厂) in Jingxian, Anhui, where all Four Treasures of calligraphy are located.
cilos: Understand the history and techniques of Chinese calligraphy.
Understand and practice various styles of calligraphy.
Understand the principles, mechanism and interaction of rice paper, ink, and brush.
Understand the applicability of media and their computational approaches to Chinese calligraphy.
Apply learned knowledge of calligraphy to creative thinking and rendering.
Develop a simple computational approach to understand or practice Chinese calligraphy.

CMAA 5008.title: Visual Communication and Expression
CMAA 5008.description: This course focuses on the arts and design of visual communication and expression with emphasis on both theory and practice. Students will learn about the design principles and techniques in visual communication and expression, develop good visual senses and relevant research skills that can inspire and enrich the creative and production process of projects that enable students to communicate and express visually and effectively.
cilos: Explain the concepts and theories of visual communication and expression.
Analyze the art and visual elements in communication.
Research visual art styles that informs future works.
Apply the skills and technique in visual communication and expression.
Design and create projects that can communicate and express visually.

CMAA 5013.title: Interactive Storytelling
CMAA 5013.description: This course explores interactive storytelling as cinematic, narrative and interactive art forms. It focuses on the art and techniques of visual storytelling that can interact thematically with the audience in meaningful ways. Students will learn about the key aspects of filmmaking and can apply narrative and interactive principles to storytelling in playable media and platform.
cilos: Explain the concepts and theories of narrative and interactivity.
Analyze the arts and techniques of cinematic interactive storytelling.
Conduct research that informs future works.
Apply the skills and techniques to interactive storytelling.
Design and create interactive narrative project.

CMAA 5014.title: Experimental 3D Rendering and Motion
CMAA 5014.description: This course examines the practice and theory of 3D computer graphics in the context of visual arts. Students will acquire the technical skills of both traditional 3D animation software programs as well as emerging real-time 3D engines, and gain a critical understanding of its technology and history. Technical instructions will be given to cover all aspects of 3D animation production, including modeling, texturing, shading, animation, lighting, and rendering. Both pioneering and emerging artists working with 3D computer images will be introduced. Lectures and discussions on other related media, including photography, film, sculpture, and installation art will also be included.
cilos: Use 3D animation software and game engine for various creative art projects.
Plan for complex 3D animation projects.
Demonstrate a critical understanding of the social implications of 3D computer.
Apply skills in 3D animation and game engine to different industries.
Critique the aesthetic and philosophical aspects of 3D rendering.
Demonstrate confidence in future studies in animation, game and VR.

CMAA 5015.title: Interactive Art: Principles and Practice
CMAA 5015.description: This course serves as an introduction to understanding interactive art and the new media art scene in general. In addition to an overview of art history concerning active audience involvement in an artwork, the course will offer a practice-led approach allowing the students to experience modalities and challenges of interactive installations. Apart from hands-on program, the course contributes to critical thinking, reflection, contextualization, and understanding different types of audience interaction modes and interfaces. The core principles and methodologies of interaction design will be introduced. In addition to that, the problematics of preservation and also presentation of the interactive artworks in the exhibition space will be addressed.
cilos: Explain the history of interactive art
Analyze different types of interactions
Know the toolset of interactive art practitioner
Demonstrate the knowledge of interface design
Know how to apply critical thinking, research tools and communication skills

CMAA 5016.title: Creative Coding
CMAA 5016.description: In this course students use well established creative coding frameworks, specifically designed for artists to program graphics, sound and interaction for generating creative work. Students will initially experiment with basic generative techniques for graphics and will then be introduced to genetic algorithms, simple machine learning for interaction, using robots to draw on paper, generating NFTs of the work they create and many more emerging technologies in order to express themselves creatively.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of creative coding frameworks.
Demonstrate the ability to develop and expand on creative coding techniques and algorithms.
Use machine learning and computer vision techniques for artists.
Apply critical thinking and communication skills.
Apply artistic creation skills.

CMAA 5017.title: AR/VR/MR/XR: Concepts, Theory and Techniques
CMAA 5017.description: This course introduces students to the concepts, theories, and interaction techniques in AR/VR/MR/XR. It covers both the fundamental concepts and design theories and the state-of-the-art interaction techniques in the field. In addition, students will work independently or in teams to design, develop, and evaluate AR/VR/MR/XR applications. In sum, by the end of the class, students will have a solid grasp of the fundamental concepts, and theories and hands-on experience in AR/VR/MR/XR.
cilos: Grasp fundamental concepts and interaction techniques in VR/AR
Apply design principles and methods to create VR/AR prototypes
Apply user-centered methods to evaluate VR/AR prototypes
Identify research gaps in the VR/AR literature
Create and evaluate VR/AR prototypes

CMAA 5018.title: Assistive Technology Design based on Computational Media and Arts
CMAA 5018.description: This course teaches students the design and evaluation of novel smart assistive technologies for people with disabilities (e.g., blind, deaf, motor-impaired) and the aging population. Students will learn user-centered methods to identify true user needs and design smart assistive technologies that leverage immersive media (e.g., VR/AR/MR) or AIoT (e.g., AI, mobile and wearable sensing). Moreover, students will also learn how to evaluate the performance and user experience of such assistive technologies.
cilos: Understand accessibility design theories and principles
Master the state-of-arts assistive technology design methods
Identify a barrier or a need of the aging population and people with disabilities
Identify a form of computational media or arts that could potentially address the barrier or the need
Design and evaluate an assistive technology prototype to address the barrier or the need
Write up the design, development, and evaluation of the assistive technology prototype

CMAA 5019.title: Machine Learning for the Arts
CMAA 5019.description: As Machine Learning (ML) permeates numerous aspects of culture, industry, and scholarship, it is crucial for the next generation of computational artists to be ML-literate, possessing the ability to critically evaluate and apply this rapidly evolving technology. Through hands-on experience with cutting-edge ML tools, students will hone their skills in this domain and establish critical perspectives on the strengths and limitations of current methods. This course employs free, open-source ML toolkits, enabling students to become familiar with various classification and regression models, RNNs, Convolutional Neural Networks, Transfer Learning, large language models, Text-to-Image generators, and more, for the purpose of implementing art projects. Each week, pertinent computational artworks utilizing various techniques are introduced, analyzed, and discussed.
cilos: Choose, implement, and reason about feature representations for data used in interactive art, music, and other creative applications, such as sensor data, audio data, image and video data, social media data, etc.

Reason about and apply machine learning and data analysis techniques (including classification, regression, and temporal modelling) to design new interactive art, music, and other creative interactions
Understand how machine learning is currently used in music, art, and other creative industries
Have a better understanding of common and popular machine learning models, how they work, how to train these models, and their use cases in creative projects.
Apply machine learning and other data analysis techniques to the creation of original works of music, art, games, or to the design of new types of interactions with digital technology

Critically engage with machine learning techniques, drawing on a technical and practical understanding of the use of these techniques, as well as on uses of these techniques in art, music, and interactive experiences
Proficiently use the ml5.js library

CMAA 5021.title: Creative Showcase Projects
CMAA 5021.description: Topics in aesthetic computing include generative art with focus on automatic generation of various styles of abstract art. Students engage in developing creative showcase projects, including program solving using visual languages, innovative visualization, generation of aesthetic images and digital art / AI art showcases. Assessment includes attendance in the class, technical presentations and report writing.
cilos: Understand how to formulate a creative project
Write a research paper and get it published
Understand various topics closely related to computational media and arts
Apply knowledge to independently develop small and deliverable showcase projects
Present ideas and results in a professional manner
Work in a team

CMAA 5022.title: Social Media for Creatives
CMAA 5022.description: This course introduces art and media students to the various online social media platforms, as well as the fundamentals of producing artistic and creative media content in collaborative group projects. The course covers a wide range of interesting topics related to art and creativity techniques and functions on social media platforms, including but not limited to: digital storytelling, games and gamification, immersive art technologies, presentation, and advertisement. By the end of this course, students will have a better understanding of art and creativity on social media platforms.
cilos: Understand how social media platforms work and evolve.
Suggest and implement many creative and artistic design ideas to improve audience engagement and marketing across a wide range of social media platforms.
Demonstrate a global outlook with respect for cultural diversity when creating social media content.
Gain a deeper understanding of the steps of social media monitoring and big data analysis using specialized graphical analysis tools like Gephi and Cytoscape.
Learn about quantitative and qualitative research methods commonly used in social media studies, such as quasi-experimental designs, content analysis, and crowdsourced survey collection.
Work collaboratively with other students and demonstrate initiative to enhance ethical values in social media platforms through appropriate disciplinary methods.
Present disciplinary knowledge, experience, and ideas about social media platforms more clearly, coherently, and with independence.

CMAA 5023.title: Programming for Virtual and Augmented Reality
CMAA 5023.description: This course introduces students to programming skills and selected topics for virtual and augmented reality (VR and AR) projects. Students will initially learn basic programming skills relating to modelling, motion controllers, animation, rendering, navigation, networking using Unity3D. Next, students will be exposed to selected topics in VR and AR, including multi-modal interactions, collaborative interactions, visual perceptions in AR, etc. By the end of the course, students will be able to create their own interactive VR and AR creative applications as a course project (games, storytelling, VR experiences, etc.).
cilos: Understand core technologies and programming skills for virtual and augmented reality (VR and AR).
Understand how VR and AR can be applied in arts, communication, and data analysis.
Have a better understanding of strengths and limitations of current VR and AR technologies, and possible solutions for the limitations.
Understand core principles and components for effective VR and AR applications.
Demonstrate how VR/AR technologies can be applied to address real-world problems.
Proficiently use the Unity3D engine.

CMAA 5024.title: Virtual Reality for the Arts
CMAA 5024.description: This course focuses on creating art projects using virtual reality (VR) technology. Students learn the fundamentals of VR-related frameworks, tools, and hardware, with specific emphasis on using a game engine to create immersive content and interaction. Students also get familiar with the historical development and contemporary examples of VR art and relevant theoretical topics, including simulation, virtual body, spatial sound, etc. The course content will include lectures and tutorials, and will be supplemented by visiting speakers, discussions and readings to provide diverse perspectives. By the end of the course, students will complete a creative VR project either individually or in teams.
cilos: Develop methods for conceptual and artistic development of virtual reality art projects.
Gain technical skills in working with game engine and virtual reality hardware.
Understand how virtual reality technology can and has been used in artistic practice.
Understand the history and recent development of virtual reality technology.
Critically discuss and critique media art projects.
Reflect philosophically on various art-theoretical aspects of virtuality and art.
Verbally communicate research and project ideas and deliver technical tutorials.

CMAA 5025.title: Computational Techniques for Sketch-based Creativity
CMAA 5025.description: This course provides an in-depth introduction to algorithms and interfaces that bridge sketching and modeling, with a particular focus on tools that support the conceptual design of shape and creation of artwork at a variety of scales. We will explore the full pipeline of concept to fabricated shape. Topics to be covered include: 2D and 3D representations, non-photorealistic rendering, sketch processing, image synthesis, sketch-based modelling, fabrication, pen and touch, and XR interfaces. We will also cover classic and cutting-edge papers published on top computer graphics and HCI venues. We will discuss how these techniques and systems benefit art and design, and vice versa.
cilos: Understand various representations of digital media, such as 2D raster and vector graphics and 3D polygon meshes.
Understand various research topics related to sketching, such as non-photorealistic rendering, sketch-based modeling, and sketch-based image synthesis.
Use existing digital techniques and systems and implement new ones for their creative practice.
Follow cutting-edge research in computer graphics and HCI and give good paper presentations.
Identify challenges in digital tools supporting creativity and propose future research directions.
Proficiently use programming frameworks for developing sketching algorithms and interfaces.

CMAA 5026.title: Art-based Research Methodologies
CMAA 5026.description: The course provides an overview into the doctoral research processes and introduces research tools for conducting art-based research. The students will explore relevant literature, familiarize themselves with methodologies, and learn how to do critical analysis of artistic practices. The course will help students advance their art-based research and teach them how to approach their practice in a systematic way. The main outcome of the course is to apply the gained understanding in improving one's own research plan for guiding one's doctoral research and funding of it.
cilos: Understand practice-based research methods and processes.
Familiarize with a variety of examples across a broad continuum of research through artistic practices including artistic research, practice-led and practice-based approaches.
Engage critically with related case studies and literature.
Apply and design practice-based or practice-led research method(s).

CMAA 5027.title: Emerging Technologies in Media, Art and Heritage
CMAA 5027.description: This course provides students with the necessary knowledge and skills to critically evaluate the role and use of emerging computational technologies in Art, Media, and Heritage. These technologies include Generative AI, Natural Language Processing, Sentiment Analysis, and others. Students will learn to select and assess these technologies based on their ability to best support the core values of art creation, media production, and heritage applications through various coursework. The course will feature real-world experience, case studies, and guest speakers to provide students with a practical understanding of these technologies. Furthermore, students will receive hands-on technical training through weekly or bi-weekly practical activities. Eventually, students will develop innovative content or applications for exhibition or real-world collaboration.

CMAA 5028.title: Immersive Authoring for World Building and Animation
CMAA 5028.description: Creating immersivity in virtual reality allows creators to have an engaging experience in creating arts, animation, or visual assets for building virtual world. The way of creating is significantly different compared to traditional methods of creating. In this studio-based course, students will be introduced creating methods using different immersive authoring tools in VR, such as QuillVR and Gravity Sketch; and have opportunities to practice the sketching, assets building, animation and pipeline building for world building projects.

CMAA 5029.title: Storyboarding and Pre-visualization for Cinematic and Immersive Content
CMAA 5029.description: Pre-visualization is an important stage for time-based and real-time projects. In this course, the instructor will introduce different pre-visualization and storyboarding techniques covering cinematic language and stage art language for screen-based projects and VR/AR projects. Traditional methods of storyboarding focusing on gaining cinematic knowledge will be introduced; and applying that, emerging techniques for storyboarding in VR will be covered with pre-visualization projects.

CMAA 5030.title: Interactive Music Systems Design
CMAA 5030.description: The course provides a comprehensive overview of the main digital sound manipulation and synthesis and their application in the design of interactive music systems. At the end of the course, students will have a solid knowledge of Pure Data, a visual programming language that can be incorporated in a number of interactive environments. Additionally, a number of research topics in the field will be explored.

CMAA 5031.title: Introduction to Game Development
CMAA 5031.description: This is a comprehensive course designed to introduce students to the fundamental aspects of game creation. Covering topics from game design principles, programming basics, art and sound design, to industry-standard software and tools, this course offers a hands-on approach to learning. Students will engage in both theoretical understanding and practical application, leading to the development of their own simple game project by the end of the course. This course is ideal for beginners aspiring to enter the field of game development and those seeking to understand the basics of this dynamic and creative industry.
cilos: Analyze and apply fundamental game design principles to create engaging gameplay experiences.
Design and develop basic 2D and 3D game environments using industry-standard game engines like Unity or Unreal Engine.
Implement basic programming concepts in a game development context using languages such as C# or JavaScript.
Create simple character models and integrate them into game settings, understanding basic principles of animation and movement.
Develop effective sound design elements, including background music and sound effects, to enhance the gaming experience.
Construct user-friendly game interfaces, considering principles of user experience (UX) and user interface (UI) design.
Plan and manage a small-scale game development project, demonstrating an understanding of the game development lifecycle from concept to testing.

CMAA 5032.title: Advanced Game Development
CMAA 5032.description: This course delves deeper into the intricacies of creating sophisticated and engaging video games. This course is designed for students who have a foundational understanding of game development and are looking to enhance their skills in areas such as advanced programming, complex game mechanics, AI integration, and immersive storytelling. Emphasizing a project-based approach, the course allows students to work on elaborate game projects, encouraging collaboration and innovation. Throughout the course, students will also explore emerging trends and technologies shaping the future of the gaming industry. This course is perfect for those aiming to refine their game development expertise and craft compelling, high-quality gaming experiences.
cilos: Design complex and engaging game narratives and worlds, demonstrating an advanced understanding of narrative design and world-building.
Apply advanced programming techniques and algorithms to optimize game performance and functionality.
Create intricate and immersive 3D environments and levels, using sophisticated design and rendering techniques.
Integrate advanced graphics and animation into game projects, showcasing proficiency in 3D modeling and visual effects.
Implement artificial intelligence algorithms to enhance gameplay and create dynamic gaming experiences.
Produce high-quality audio elements, including soundtracks and sound effects, for a professional-level gaming experience.
Develop and manage complex game projects, demonstrating skills in teamwork, project management, and understanding of the gaming industry's business aspects.

CMAA 5033.title: Computational Media and Arts Theory I
CMAA 5033.description: This course delves into the critical exploration of cultural and philosophical theories that underpin the evolving landscape of computational media arts. It immerses students in relevant readings and discussions, providing them with a deep understanding of the complex interplay between humanities, science, technology, culture, and art. Through the examination of key texts and critical debates, students will engage with concepts that shape the field, such as digital aesthetics, media archaeology, cybernetics, posthumanism, and the impact of technology on society.
cilos: Acquire a strong foundation in cultural and media theories related to computational arts, providing the intellectual tools necessary for meaningful discourse on technology, culture, and art.
Engage in critical thinking and analysis of cultural and philosophical theories related to computational media arts, fostering a deeper understanding of their implications for artistic practice.
Contextualize computational artworks within broader cultural and philosophical contexts, enabling a nuanced appreciation of the cultural and ethical dimensions of digital creations.
Explore ethical considerations related to technology and media arts, fostering an awareness of the ethical responsibilities of artists in a digital age.
Integrate theoretical insights into creative practice, enabling the creation of computationally driven artworks that are culturally and philosophically resonant.
Cultivate the habit of critical self-reflection, and evaluate their own work in light of theoretical concepts, leading to more profound and thought-provoking artistic creations.

CMAA 5034.title: Computational Media and Arts Theory II
CMAA 5034.description: This course represents the advanced level of critical exploration and intellectual growth in the realm of computational media arts. Building upon the foundations established in CMAA 5033, this course delves deeper into the theoretical dimensions of the field while placing a heightened emphasis on honing students' theoretical and reflective writing skills. Through an engaging blend of readings, discussions, and writing assignments, this course empowers students to not only grasp complex theoretical concepts but also articulate their insights with clarity and precision through reflective writing in relation to their artistic practice, preparing students for thesis writing.
cilos: Develop an advanced understanding of complex theoretical frameworks relevant to computational media arts.
Critically analyze and evaluate advanced theoretical concepts in the context of computational media arts, enabling a deeper comprehension of their implications for artistic practice.
Synthesize and integrate diverse theoretical perspectives to form coherent and original insights that contribute to the advancement of discourse in the field.
Hone advanced reflective writing skills to express complex ideas, theories, and critical analyses with clarity, coherence, and precision.
Explore advanced research methodologies relevant to computational media arts, laying the groundwork for in-depth academic and creative inquiry.
Engage in scholarly discourse and peer review, fostering the ability to provide constructive feedback and contribute to the academic and artistic community.

CMAA 5035.title: Procedural Modeling for Content Generation
CMAA 5035.description: This course provides an in-depth introduction to procedural modeling with a focus on algorithms and applications. Procedural modeling techniques use computer-generated randomness and processing power to create content algorithmically as opposed to manually. Through critical reading and hands-on exercise, students will explore the value of procedural content generation in art, design, education, movies, and games.

CMAA 5036.title: e-Textiles and Wearable Technology
CMAA 5036.description: This course will integrate electronic technologies for signals and light, programming of computer embroidery machines, and explore new textile manufacturing technologies. The class is grounded in project-based learning, combined with reading and discussion of research papers. We will create and exhibit wearable and/or portable eTextile items as final projects.

CMAA 5037.title: Social Robots for HCI, Art, and Design
CMAA 5037.description: This course reimagines human-robot interaction (HRI) through the lenses of human-computer interaction (HCI), speculative design, and artistic practice, centering creativity, empathy, and critical inquiry over technical implementation. Students will have hands-on opportunities to work directly with a few types of robotics, including but not limited to robotics arms, dogs, small swarms, drones, and so on. Through implementing a robotics prototype for human-robot interaction purposes, this course will lead students to explore how social robots amplify human agency, foster collaboration and artistic creation, and challenge societal norms in spaces ranging from homes and hospitals to galleries and public installations. The course will cover both theoretical and technical foundations through seminars, discussions of cutting-edge research papers, technical tutorials, and collaborative work on an empirical, practical, or creative robotics research project.
cilos: Understand key theories and interdisciplinary perspectives in human-robot interaction (HRI), speculative design, and artistic practice, and how they shape the design and societal impact of social robots.
Apply research and design methodologies such as speculative design, Wizard-of-Oz prototyping, participatory design, and research through design to explore innovative human-robot interactions.
Acquire practical skills in designing and prototyping social robot interactions, utilizing creative approaches from art experiments, embodied interaction, and performance-based robotics.

Engage with contemporary research and case studies to analyze power dynamics, cultural influences, and ethical considerations in human-robot relationships across caregiving, surveillance, and creative applications.
Articulate research findings and design concepts through academic writing, speculative scenarios, artistic documentation, and oral presentations
Gain hands-on experience in prototyping human-robot interactions using accessible hardware and software tools, integrating HCI principles, embodied AI, and creative robotics techniques.

CMAA 5038.title: The Hybrid Studio: Art x AI x Engineering
CMAA 5038.description: This hands-on course brings together artists, engineers, and multidisciplinary creators to solve real-world challenges through collaborative problem-solving. Teams will leverage AI tools for rapid ideation and prototyping, alongside human-centered design thinking, iterative testing, and artistic critique. The curriculum explores how AI can enhance cross-disciplinary workflows while emphasizing ethical co-creation, hybrid human-machine creativity, and tangible outcomes that merge technical with artistic vision. Final projects will be showcased publicly through exhibitions, installations, or live demonstrations.
cilos: Demonstrate effective teamwork between art and engineering perspectives.
Negotiate trade-offs between creative vision and technical feasibility.
Conduct user research, prototype iteratively, and validate solutions through public exhibitions or field tests.
Leverage generative AI for ideation/prototyping while auditing for bias, over-reliance, and ethical implications.
Produce installed works or functional prototypes that meet professional standards for durability, safety, and audience engagement.
Present projects to both technical and artistic juries using appropriate visual, verbal, and technical documentation.

CMAA 5040.title: Sensor Technologies in Computational Arts and HCI
CMAA 5040.description: This course offers practical methods for designing and developing interactive techniques using off-the-shelf sensors, focusing on creative experiences like art creation and spatial interaction in computational arts and HCI. Students will gain hands-on experience throughout the entire process of developing sensor-based interaction methods and applications. The course, structured around case studies, covers sensor data collection, data organization, signal processing, and the use of machine learning to create engaging, responsive systems.
cilos: Have an overall understanding of state-of-the-art interactive techniques, including their working principles (hardware & algorithms), application scenarios, and future development trends.
Understand the development lifecycle of modern interactive techniques, including data gathering, signal processing, machine learning model deployment, and system evaluation.
Master basic signal processing methods and algorithms for different types of sensor data (e.g., visual, acoustic, inertial, and touch sensor data).
Apply machine learning and signal processing methods to create novel interactive experience for art creation, spatial interaction, physiological computing, etc.
Develop interactive systems based on off-the-shelf boards (Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense) and sensors (IMU, camera, microphone, etc.).
Understand design and evaluation methods for interactive techniques.
Form critical thinking on the social impacts and human factors of modern interactive technology.

CMAA 5041.title: Experiment Design for Protocol Optimization
CMAA 5041.description: This course is for students who want to improve their skills in designing and optimizing experiment protocol in HCI study. It focuses on helping students understand the difference between exploring new ideas and confirming what we already know. The course covers key concepts like how to plan experiments, test different variables, and find the best solutions using advanced techniques to verify their new interaction protocol. Students will also learn both quantitative (numbers-based) and qualitative (observation-based) research methods, giving them a strong foundation for conducting experiments. Along with learning how to design experiments, students will get hands on experience with statistical tools to analyze data and make informed decisions. By the end of the course, students will be confident in using these methods to solve real-world problems and improve processes in different areas of research.
cilos: Design and implement experiments systematically to explore new creative ideas in computational media and arts.
Apply optimization techniques to improve the efficiency and quality of their creative processes and projects.
Utilize statistical tools for data analysis and interpretation to make informed decisions in their creative work.
Evaluate the effectiveness of experimental projects and draw meaningful insights from data.
Demonstrate proficiency in using experimental design and system development principles to drive innovation and continuous improvement in individual research work.

CMAA 5042.title: Immersive Cinema
CMAA 5042.description: In this course we will explore the artistic, formal, and technical processes involved in creating motion pictures for non-standard screens and multi-channel, immersive cinema installations that occupy a unique, multi-projection cinema architecture. We will create work that expands cinema from passively viewed, two-dimensional projection in a traditional theater architecture to an embodied, poly-perspectival configuration of cinema in space. Approaching cinema as a form of concrete poetry, we will investigate the potential for expression and meaning-making rooted within the specificity of different formal presentation formats to develop an individual language of expression.
cilos: Demonstrate technical and historical knowledge and skills of immersive cinema as a medium and artform.
Create an original immersive cinematic artwork utilizing advanced technology and techniques.
Demonstrate advanced critical thinking, creativity, and effective oral communication, while clearly articulating in writing the ideas and processes underlying their creative practice.
Conduct independent, original artistic, and theoretical research within the field of media arts.
Utilize state-of-the-art technology for cinematic creation.
Plan, design, and realize large-scale projects in computational art.
Demonstrate mastery of foundational theories, key historical developments, and representative examples of contemporary moving-image media art and related technologies.

CMAA 5043.title: Creative Prototyping: Designing Interactive Experiences
CMAA 5043.description: This course offers a comprehensive introduction to UX/interfaces/interaction design methods with a focus on prototyping interactive and intelligent interfaces and systems. Students will explore core design theories, human-centered design principles, and gain hands-on experience in developing prototypes using web frameworks and generative AI tools. Through a combination of seminars, practical design sessions, and a final project, students will acquire the technical and critical thinking skills needed to create innovative, interactive, and intelligent technologies.
cilos: Develop a deep understanding of the fundamental theories and principles of interface design and interaction design, and how they inform the design and evaluation of interactive computing technologies.
Gain proficiency in human-centered design methodologies and create user-centered interactive systems that effectively meet the needs of diverse user populations.
Acquire practical skills in rapid prototyping techniques, platforms, and programming languages.

Engage with contemporary research in interactive and intelligent interfaces through academic readings, presentations, and discussions, and critically evaluate existing work and identify opportunities for innovation.
Articulate research findings and design insights clearly and effectively, both in written form (e.g., research papers) and through presentations.
Proficiently develop interactive interfaces via web frameworks, Cursor, and generative AI technologies.

CMAA 5045.title: Digital Fabrication and Physical Computing
CMAA 5045.description: Interactive physical devices are a cornerstone of contemporary media art. The course addresses this field by introducing students to a suite of essential tools and processes, including 3D printing, laser cutting, CNC milling, electronics, coding, and circuit design. Through a hands-on, project-based approach, students will develop foundational skills in prototyping. Under the instructor's guidance, they will progress step-by-step through the design and creation of their own interactive, electronic objects. Graded P or F.
cilos: Understand the fundamental role of physical computing in contemporary arts.
Formulate and develop design concepts centered around a physical device.
Program a microcontroller and implement the mapping of sensors and actuators.
Acquire foundational knowledge and skills in Computer-Aided Design (CAD).
Acquire foundational knowledge and skills in Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM).
Operate a variety of digital fabrication machines.

CMAA 5046.title: Hypercinemas: Fulldome, 360°-Cinema, and Beyond
CMAA 5046.description: This course introduces the practice, theory, and history of 360° fulldome cinema, emphasizing hands-on experimentation alongside critical inquiry. Students will explore hemispherical cinematography and animation, hemispheric optics, spatial audio, and somatic montage, while investigating how images, sound, and architectonic space shape immersive spectatorship. Approaching cinema as a hyper-medium and a form of concrete poetry, the course examines how meaning emerges through spatialized representation, temporality, embodied perception, and the interplay of art, science, and technology. Throughout the semester, students develop 2D and 3D image and sound techniques to compose “in the round,” culminating in an original immersive work for fulldome exhibition.

Create an original fulldome cinematic artwork utilizing advanced technologies and techniques.
Demonstrate advanced critical thinking, creativity and effective oral communication, while clearly articulating in writing the ideas and processes underlying their creative practice.
Conduct independent, original artistic, and theoretical research within the field of immersive cinema.
Utilize state-of-the-art technology for artistic creation.
Plan, design, and realize large-scale projects in computational art.
Demonstrate mastery of foundational theories, key historical developments, and representative examples of contemporary moving-image media art and related technologies.

CMAA 6020.title: Group Critique
CMAA 6020.description: Group Critique fosters critical thinking and collaborative engagement among students. In this course, participants engage in a structured environment where they present their ongoing computational arts projects for peer review and feedback. Through constructive discussions and critiques, students learn to evaluate and analyze their work within the context of contemporary media arts, technology, and cultural discourse. They develop the essential skills of articulating their artistic intentions, receiving constructive criticism, and providing thoughtful assessments of their peers' projects. Group Critique serves as a vital forum for refining ideas, enhancing artistic practices, and cultivating a deeper understanding of the role of computation in art and culture. Students are required to take this course in each regular term and for at least three terms. Graded PP, P or F.
cilos: Provide constructive and insightful feedback on their peers' computational arts projects, emphasizing clarity, specificity, and sensitivity to artistic intent.
Enhance their skill in articulating their own artistic intentions to refine their creative processes and clarify the conceptual underpinnings of their work.

Foster critical thinking skills in discussions that explore the cultural, technological, and conceptual aspects of computational media arts, encouraging a deeper understanding of the field's broader context.
Develop a professional mindset, preparing for careers in computational media arts where effective communication and collaboration are essential skills.

Develop the capacity for introspection and self-assessment, honing their ability to critically evaluate their own work in response to peer feedback, and thereby fostering continuous artistic improvement.
Broaden their perspectives and gain a more comprehensive understanding of the various approaches and styles within the field, enriching their own creative practice.

CMAA 6700.title: Internship in Computational Arts I
CMAA 6700.description: The guaranteed internship offers students the opportunity to further explore their creative boundaries in an alternative environment within the realm of computational media arts. The internship empowers students to embark on artistic journeys in a context beyond the regular learning environment within academic institutions, providing fresh guidance and new resources to experiment with new ideas, technologies, and processes. CMAA 6991.title: MFA Thesis Project I
CMAA 6991.description: The MFA Thesis Project in Computational Arts is a culmination of the student's creative and technical journey, embodying their unique vision at the intersection of art and technology. This intensive project requires students to conceptualize and realize a significant piece of work that pushes the boundaries of digital art, integrating coding, digital media, and interactive technologies. Guided by faculty mentors, students will demonstrate mastery in their chosen area, be it interactive installations, digital fabrication, VR/AR experiences, or generative art, culminating in a public exhibition and a comprehensive written thesis that contextualizes their work within contemporary artistic discourse. In Part I, students will establish a direction in their practice and do an extensive literature review of their specific field. Graded P or F.
cilos: Integrate and synthesize theoretical and practical knowledge of computational arts, applying it effectively in the creation of an innovative project.
Conduct comprehensive research, employing appropriate methodologies to explore and inform the conceptual and technical aspects of their project.
Exhibit advanced proficiency in computational tools and techniques, applying them skillfully in the execution of their artistic vision.
Articulate the conceptual underpinnings of their project, critically analyze and contextualize their work within the broader field of computational arts.
Successfully present their project in a public exhibition, demonstrating clear communication skills and the ability to engage with critical feedback.

CMAA 6993.title: MFA Thesis Exhibition
CMAA 6993.description: This is a capstone course designed for students in the Master of Fine Arts in Computational Arts program, focusing on the practical and organizational aspects of staging an exhibition. This course offers hands-on experience in exhibition planning, space management, curation, and publicity, providing students with the necessary skills to effectively showcase their computational art projects. Through this immersive experience, students will learn to navigate the complexities of exhibition design, from conceptualization to execution, ensuring their artistic visions are communicated effectively to the public. This course does not center on creating artworks; instead, it emphasizes the behind-the-scenes processes essential for successful art exhibitions. Graded P or F.
